advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the line-458 out-of-sync logger so it only fires on a genuine detected divergence (both SHAs present and differing), not on the failed-comparison oos=1 path which already logs at line 451.
evidence: 449:  # Could not compare. Report the breaching value rather than staying silent (see above).
451:  logger -t rebar-health "mirror sync check failed, publishing mirror_out_of_sync=1 (gerrit='${gerrit_sha}' github='${github_sha}')"

On the failed path gerrit_sha and/or github_sha are empty, so line 458 logs 'mirror out-of-sync: gerrit= github=' — a divergence-shaped message with no SHAs, duplicating the failure already logged at 451.
advisory.finding: On the failed-comparison path (oos=1 set in the else branch), observability.sh emits TWO journald lines describing the same event: the accurate diagnostic at line 451 ('mirror sync check failed, publishing mirror_out_of_sync=1 (gerrit=... github=...)') and then the unconditional out-of-sync line at 458 ('mirror out-of-sync: gerrit=${gerrit_sha} github=${github_sha}') which fires because oos>0 but prints EMPTY SHAs, misrepresenting a fetch failure as a detected divergence with blank operands.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change line 458 to only log on a real comparison mismatch, e.g. gate it on non-empty SHAs: `[ -n "$gerrit_sha" ] && [ -n "$github_sha" ] && [ "$oos" -gt 0 ] && logger ...`, leaving the failed-fetch case to its dedicated line 451.

evidence: observability.sh publishes every 5 minutes (probe timer), so a 900s alarm period sums three publishes; only three consecutive missed publishes empty a period.

monitoring_autodeploy.tf:188-191 rationale: 'with treat_missing_data = "breaching" below a single absent period would page, and absent periods are ordinary timer jitter' — this jitter model is the 300s-period model, not the 900s one.
This is a documentation/rationale accuracy concern, not a config defect: the resulting 2-of-4 window is conservative and safe.
dropped.finding: The flap-widening rationale on the 900s-period autodeploy/foxterrier alarms is copied from the 300s alarms and asserts that '~22 of 24 periods present' / 'a single absent period would page' motivates the wider window, but with period=900 the Sum statistic aggregates three 5-minute publishes per period, so a single missed 5-minute publish does NOT produce a missing 900s period. The stated jitter mechanism does not apply at 900s the way the comment claims.
